PortfolioProject.title: PortfolioProject
PortfolioProject.description: Represents a portfolio project showcased by AMpire Studio.

id.description: Unique identifier for the PortfolioProject entity.

serviceType.description: Type of service provided in the project (e.g., Web Design, Animation).

projectHighlights.description: AI-generated highlights summarizing the project's key value points.

cmsId.description: Reference to CMS content. (Relationship: CMS 1:1 PortfolioProject)

CMSContent.title: CMSContent
CMSContent.description: Represents content managed by the Sanity CMS.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CMSContent entity.

content.description: The actual content managed by the CMS, stored as a string (e.g., JSON, Markdown).

lastUpdated.description: Timestamp of the last content update.

definition.description: Stores portfolio project data.  No denormalized fields needed, as authorization is open. `{projectId}` corresponds to the 'id' field in the PortfolioProject schema.

params.name: projectId
params.description: Unique identifier for the portfolio project.

definition.description: Stores CMS content. No denormalized fields needed, as authorization is open. `{contentId}` corresponds to the 'id' field in the CMSContent schema.

params.name: contentId
params.description: Unique identifier for the CMS content.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to manage portfolio projects and associated CMS content for AMpire Studio. It prioritizes authorization independence and simplifies security rules.

`/portfolio_projects`: This collection stores the main portfolio project data.  It supports QAPs because listing all projects requires no authorization checks (the data is assumed to be public).  The schema for `PortfolioProject` ensures a predictable data structure.

`/cms_content`:  This collection stores the CMS content, and is related to the `PortfolioProject` data through the `cmsId` field. Like projects, this collection is designed for public access.

Authorization Independence: Both collections are designed to avoid hierarchical authorization. Since there are no ownership or role-based restrictions, every document can be accessed by anyone.
